lessons.situation: A contractor has replied to a quote request for check-out remedial works (replacing non-working lights and a water-damaged ceiling board), and the job is on hold awaiting the provider; the quote needs landlord sign-off before works can proceed.
lessons.action: When a contractor's quote arrives for a job on hold 'waiting for provider', treat it as the cue to act rather than just returning the job to auto: send the landlord a concise email summarising the scope as per the check-out report, the quoted price (stating whether VAT is excluded), and a clear request for permission to proceed. Then place the job on hold with the reason 'waiting for landlord'.
lessons.rationale: The quote is the blocker for the provider hold; the next dependency is the landlord's approval of the cost, so the hold reason must be updated and the landlord asked explicitly so that the job does not stall or proceed without authorisation.

lessons.situation: A checkout-clean request was auto-paused because the property is vacant (not tenanted), a contractor was asked to quote against the checkout report, and the contractor then replied confirming the quote has been sent.
lessons.action: When the contractor confirms their quote has been sent after a vacant-property pause, review the quote against the checkout report scope and forward it to the landlord for approval, stating that the clean is chargeable to the outgoing tenant and asking whether the contractor may proceed. Then put the job on hold as 'Waiting for Landlord' rather than returning it to auto mode, and do not send a further reply to the contractor.
lessons.rationale: A vacant-property pause needs manual handling, and the quote must have landlord sign-off before the contractor is instructed, so the job should wait on the landlord instead of resuming automatic processing.

lessons.situation: After several reminders to a contractor about booking a check-out works visit, the contractor replies with an itemised quote for the work but no appointment details, and the request had been put on hold for a quote.
lessons.action: Treat the contractor's reply as the awaited quote rather than a scheduling confirmation. Forward the itemised quote to the landlord, listing each line item and its price, and ask explicitly for approval to instruct the contractor so the property can be made ready for remarketing. Keep the request on hold until the landlord replies, and do not instruct the contractor or return the job to auto mode before approval is received.
lessons.rationale: Quote-based works need landlord sign-off before the contractor proceeds, and a contractor reply that contains a quote means the chasing for an appointment has been superseded by the approval step.

lessons.situation: After a quote was sent to the landlord for approval and chased once, the landlord replied with only a thumbs-up emoji and the request was flagged to check whether a response was needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Treat a brief affirmative reply such as a thumbs-up emoji as landlord approval of the quote already put to them. Do not send the landlord a further response. Instead, instruct the contractor straight away to proceed at the quoted price, restating the work and the quoted cost, then put the job on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Provider' until the contractor confirms scheduling or completion.
lessons.rationale: The landlord's approval was clear and nothing further was needed from them, so the next step is to move the job forward with the contractor rather than ask for clarification or return the job to auto mode.

lessons.situation: A landlord replied to a repair request saying they will sort the issue themselves with their own contractor, so the agency no longer needs to arrange works but still needs to know when the job is done.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply to check whether it needs a response; if it only confirms they will handle the repair, send no further reply. Put the request on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Landlord' and a comment saying it is held awaiting the landlord's contractor to complete. If the tenant or landlord later gives no update, chase the landlord politely for progress and keep the hold in place until the contractor reports completion.
lessons.rationale: When the landlord takes ownership of the repair, the agency's role changes from instructing works to monitoring them, so the request must stay paused rather than return to auto mode, and the landlord must be chased so the job does not stall unnoticed.

input.message:
Dear Landlord,

Re: 27 Thistle Lane, Brackley Vale, ZZ3 9ZZ – bedroom radiator not heating (ref R/12)

Thank you for approving the repair with Harlow Heating up to £150. We contacted Harlow, and they are fully booked until 3 November. They have offered an emergency visit sooner, but at double their normal rate. They haven't given us a price for that.

We also have a quote from another firm, Quick Fix Heating. They can attend on Monday 6 October to inspect the radiator and replace the valve for £230 including parts. That is £80 above your £150 limit, and it isn't Harlow, so we have not booked them.

The rest of the house is heating normally, but the bedroom is cold. Please tell us which option you'd like:
1. Wait for Harlow Heating's first standard slot from 3 November (within your £150 limit).
2. Ask Harlow Heating for a price for an emergency visit at double rate. We will come back to you with the figure before booking anything.
3. Approve Quick Fix Heating to attend on Monday 6 October for £230 including parts. Reply APPROVE to go ahead with this one.

We won't instruct anyone until we hear from you.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team

input.subject: Bedroom radiator – 27 Thistle Lane (ref R/12)
input.body:
Hello,

Here's an update on the bedroom radiator at 27 Thistle Lane, Brackley Vale (ref R/12). The landlord's preferred heating engineer can't come soon, so we have sent the landlord some other options and are waiting for their decision. Nothing is booked yet. We'll update you as soon as they reply, and we'll chase them by 6 October if we haven't heard back.

In the meantime, please check that the valve on that radiator is fully open. That's the numbered head or knob at the side of the radiator, which should be turned to its highest setting. If you have a radiator key and feel comfortable doing it, you can also try bleeding the radiator. Please let us know if that makes any difference. If anyone in the household is vulnerable to the cold, or the heating stops working anywhere else in the house, please tell us straight away.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team
